setup.scope: This market covers smartwatches as finished consumer wearable devices that run a general-purpose or wearable operating system (e.g., watchOS, Wear OS, Tizen, RTOS-based smartwatch platforms) and provide on-wrist computing, connectivity, and sensor-based functions such as notifications, fitness/health tracking, and app support. It includes standalone and Bluetooth-tethered smartwatches sold to end users through all channels (direct, e-commerce, retail), but excludes traditional mechanical/quartz watches, basic fitness bands and activity trackers without a smartwatch OS/app ecosystem, smartwatch accessories and replacement straps sold separately, and the separately valued upstream components (displays, SoCs, sensors, batteries) and software/services revenue. Component and software/service demand may still be used as intermediate evidence to derive how many smartwatch units are required, but those components and services are never priced or valued as part of this market.

setup.scope: This market covers smartwatches as finished consumer wearable devices that pair with a smartphone or operate standalone and deliver notifications, health/fitness tracking, and app-based functionality on the wrist; it includes both classic (phone-tethered) and standalone/cellular smartwatches across all price bands, display technologies (LCD, OLED/AMOLED), and operating systems (watchOS, Wear OS, Tizen, RTOS-based, etc.). Excluded are traditional mechanical/quartz analog watches, basic fitness bands and activity trackers without app-capable smartwatch functionality, smartwatch accessories and replacement straps sold separately, and the separately valued upstream components (SoCs, displays, sensors, batteries) and downstream software/services revenue (app subscriptions, cellular data plans) that are not the smartwatch device itself. Unit volumes are counted as finished smartwatch devices shipped/sold to end users, not components, packs, or accessory bundles.
